checks.action: Do NOT raise the weight or the margin. Two runs have now moved this decision monotonically the WRONG way at inference: margin 1.0 took the median gap -2.88 -> -3.75, margin 3.0 took it -2.88 -> -4.97, while gold-row separation moved correctly both times (+0.105, +0.40). Teacher-forced supervision makes the model a sharper discriminator of gold WRITE vs gold WAIT contexts, and at inference its own error-containing ASR history classifies as WAIT, so sharpening amplifies the wrong side. This decision needs either a true roll-in form -- supervised on the model's own generated ASR/MT text, which the current task pool does not contain, since boundary_rollin_rate substitutes semantic tokens only -- or it stays an inference-side calibrated bias. Note the bias itself is damaged by such a run: delta_cont=4 gives WRITE_MT 0.947 on iter_0002264 but only 0.347 here, because +4 no longer crosses -4.97.
